text: In every large-scale coherent Ising machine demonstrated to date, where is the spin-spin coupling term (the sum of J_ij times c_j) actually computed?
choices: Optically, by direct interference among the OPO pulses
In an electronic FPGA via a digital multiply-accumulate, with DAC/ADC conversion, using measurement feedback
In a superconducting quantum annealer coupled to the ring
explanation: The celebrated 'optical' Ising machine performs its defining coupling operation in an electronic FPGA via measurement feedback, so its throughput and energy are set by the electronics (homodyne detection, DAC/ADC, and an O(N^2) accumulation per round trip), not by the light. Optical delay-line interference fixes only hardwired topologies; PCM crossbars and quantum annealers are unrelated architectures.
